lesson.menu_desc: A bridge closes and the regulator wants a timeline by six: time clauses and sequence -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 19 -- Precision Under Pressure
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Aguinaldo Ballon | Lesson 19 -- Precision Under Pressure
lesson.grammar_point: future time clauses with as soon as, once, until and by the time for timelines under pressure

listenings.text: In a crisis, the first hour decides almost everything. Here is my sequence. First, find out the facts, but do not wait until you know everything. As soon as you have the basic facts, inform the people who need to know: the regulator, your board, your insurer. Second, give a time frame. Say when you will send the next update, and then send it on time, even if there is no news. Third, never guess. If someone asks a question and you do not know the answer, say: I will come back to you by four o'clock. People forgive a problem. They do not forgive silence.

I worked at a transport agency for twelve years. When a concessionaire sends us a timeline after an incident, we read three things. First, did they act before or after we called? By the time we call, a good company has already acted. Second, are the times exact? In the afternoon is not a time. At three fifteen is a time. Third, is there an interim solution? Closing a bridge is easy. Keeping a region moving until the bridge reopens is the real job. Companies that escalate problems early almost never get a penalty. Companies that hide them almost always do.

Traffic on the highway is moving again this morning after a bridge near Rio Claro was closed for about thirty-six hours. Engineers found a crack in the structure on Tuesday afternoon, and the concessionaire closed the bridge immediately. In the meantime, trucks used an old regional road, which added roughly forty minutes to each trip. The national transport agency said the company had informed it promptly and had sent a clear timeline. Permanent repairs will start next month. Until they are finished, heavy trucks will only be allowed to cross the bridge at night.
